text:
Alex: heads-up — started seeing gradual KV page growth on Dedicated (reserved GPUs) during long interactive sessions. eviction goes from clean to thrash around ~45M tokens, latency spikes. :eyes:
Maria: which cluster? logs?
Alex: dedicated-prod-eu. attaching vmstat snippet shortly. not sure if it's config drift or something at the kernel level.
Sam: can you repro on Hosted? if not, could be VPC MTU / kernel flags / numa settings on Private/onprem that change page alignment.
Infra-bot: [alert] kvcache-evict-rate increased on dedicated-prod-eu at 2024-04-12T09:22Z — OOM survivors: 3.
Jordan: did a flamegraph profile earlier — looks like slab reclaim + page-fragment sweep hot in the path that handles KV page allocation for long seqs. linked the profile: https://gist.github.com/redwood/perf-kv-1717
Lee: FYI we landed a batching heuristic tweak last week (PR #4821) that nudges larger requests into dedicated batches. might change allocation timestamps which affects KV warmth.
Olivia: that batching change was on hosted and dedicated, but Private builds had an older quant/kernel combo. could be a mismatch.
Maria: any quick repro steps?
Alex: repro steps (run from a machine in eu-west):
```
# simulate long chat to warm KV
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
  -d '{"model":"rwd-3b-kv","prompt":"a" * 500000, "max_tokens":1024}'
```
Observe `rss` and `/proc/slabinfo` growth. I can share a log snippet.
Jordan: commit c1a4be9 seems correlated with a kernel selection fallback change (we started preferring mm/madvise path A on Dedicated). that commit changed `kernel_selector` to prefer fast-path for small frames; maybe it backfired for very long contexts.
Sam: interesting — on Private (onprem) we also bind GPU memory with numa_interleave which fragments pages differently. NVLINK setups can cause different physical locality and different hugepage behavior.
Lee: can we try forcing the fallback kernel on Dedicated to match Hosted and see if growth stops? sysctl idea: `sysctl vm.nr_hugepages=0` isn't ideal but we can toggle kernel_selector via: `echo fallbackA > /sys/module/kernel_selector/parameters/mode` (placeholder)
Olivia: I ran a canary on Hosted with the previous batching heuristic and didn't see growth. difference matrix: Hosted (old kernel selector), Dedicated (new selector), Private (old selector + numa).
Maria: if we can toggle on Dedicated safely, let's do a small canary (1 node) and run Alex's repro. if it stabilizes, rollback the selector change in the next deploy.
Alex: I can run the microbench and collect `perf`, `slabinfo`, `numastat`. attaching a short tail of `/proc/slabinfo`:
```
kmalloc-1024  512 640 0 0 0 0 0
page_cache  123456 124000 0 0 0 0 0
kv_page_entry  524288 600000 0 0 0 0 0
```
Jordan: that's classic fragmentation — many partial slab pages. suggests allocator churn not true leakage. we should enable the compact heuristic and run `echo 1 > /proc/sys/vm/compact_memory` during repro.
Sam: note that VPC MTU differences (9000 vs 1500) changed average packet sizes for our prefetch path and we saw slightly different request batching behavior, which could explain why Hosted vs Dedicated diverge. not convinced it's purely kernel_selector.
Lee: action items: 1) Alex to run repro + collect perf+slab on Dedicated canary 2) Infra to flip kernel_selector on one node 3) Devex to roll back batching tweak on a small subset if needed 4) Jordan to add slab-compact toggle to perf harness.
Alex: starting repro now on canary node dedicated-prod-eu-03. will post logs in ~30m. :thumbsup:
Maria: thanks — if it looks good, we can cut a rollback. otherwise Jordan + Sam, can you pair on a deeper allocator trace?
Jordan: yea, I'll instrument the reclaim path and capture `kmem_cache` alloc/free stacks.
Infra-bot: deploy job #deploy-872 queued for kernel-selector flip on dedicated-prod-eu-03 (manual approval required).
Alex: approved and kicked off. will paste results when ready.
Olivia: dropping a note in the PR with observed differences and linking this thread.
Sam: good triage. might be multi-factor: batching heuristics change allocation cadence + kernel selector change + numa / mtu environmental differences. isolate one variable at a time.
Alex: agreed. thanks everyone.
